text: “Average high tide” is Mean Higher High Water (MHHW): the average of each day’s highest tide at the NOAA tide gauge in {station}, {mhhw} ft NAVD88. Tides above it reach farther onto low shorelines, marshes and trails. Based on NOAA tide measurements, NOAA’s model forecast and the predicted (astronomical) tide.

text: MHHW (Mean Higher High Water) is the average height of the highest tide each day. Tides above it reach farther up shorelines, marshes and low-lying areas than usual.

NOAA forecast is model guidance from NOAA's San Francisco Bay Operational Forecast System: the water level at this gauge including wind, air pressure and river flow, about 2 days ahead, updated 4 times a day. It is not an official forecast; NWS advisories take precedence.

text: King Tide dates from San Mateo County Emergency Management, “Tide days of concern, Oct 2026 to Apr 2027.” They are astronomical tide predictions for NOAA’s San Francisco gauge (9414290) and don’t include weather. Redwood City tides usually run higher than San Francisco, and storms, wind and runoff can add more, so check the Redwood City predictions and NWS alerts for the actual forecast.

text: Flooding likely: move away from the creek and low areas now.
Be ready: the creek could flood. Be ready to move to higher ground.
Stay alert: conditions are getting worse. Avoid creek banks and check back often.
No alerts: nothing unusual right now. Conditions can change quickly in a storm.
The bar shows where the creek is between its normal level and its flood level, measured at a creek gauge. The marker is the latest reading.
Rain is compared with how often that much rain falls at the same gauge: Heavy (about once a year), Very heavy (about once every two years), Intense (about once every five years).
notes: Levels from NOAA Atlas 14 (rain_frequency.csv)

text: Rain levels: Heavy = at least a 1-year storm for some duration at that gauge, Very heavy = 2-year, Intense = 5-year (NOAA Atlas 14). Storm size and chance in any year are for the heaviest window. Supporting = a hillside gauge that counts toward the creek's rain level but isn't in its rain tables. Trigger = a rain (and tide) rule in thresholds.csv.
